title: Leaving devices, medicines, and equipment for trained staff after death

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source practice-layer synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe recognized care patterns but do not supply firsthand room texture.
This record must not become procedure-level instruction for a particular death.
Treatment, legal, ritual, emergency, and equipment decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: After death, there may be medicines, syringe drivers, catheters, oxygen equipment, dressings, or other devices in the room, and witnesses are unsure what to remove, return, or leave alone.
ordinary_language_queries: syringe driver after death what to do

content_layers.observation_text: After-death professional guidance includes attention to medicines, devices, documentation, and who should remove or manage them; family-facing sources generally route these questions to staff and planned contacts.
content_layers.source_synthesis: Marie Curie’s professional material and public after-death checklists support an equipment/medicine boundary record: preserve the scene’s practical reality but do not instruct untrained readers to handle devices.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: The modern dying room contains machines, tubes, medicines, forms, and chargers. A bedside atlas that ignores equipment will feel false; one that instructs equipment handling will be unsafe.

what_this_is_not: not a substitute for hospice, district nurse, doctor, pharmacy, funeral, or equipment-provider guidance
uncertainties: Device and medication rules vary by jurisdiction, service, prescription, and home/facility setting.
Controlled medicines, sharps, oxygen, and implanted or external devices may have special rules.
Sudden or reportable deaths require separate evidence-preservation/legal pathways.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should acknowledge that equipment and medicines may remain in the room and tell readers to follow their care plan or contact the relevant team before moving or disposing of anything.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect handoff checklists, family explanations, and safe phrasing around devices, medicines, returns, and what not to touch.
language_notes: Use “leave for trained staff” unless a reviewed local source says otherwise.
Do not describe drugs or devices in operational detail beyond source-supported orientation.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the practice layer. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, not a legal instruction, not a ritual authority, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical or domain review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent, worried, legal, medication, swallowing, equipment, or body-handling questions to qualified local support.
